spec_match.rationale: Demonstrates the motivating trade-off — credentials in the handshake versus the first message, including the unproven-session window — but necessarily measures it over fetch/WebSocket stand-ins because this host cannot serve HTTP/3 WebTransport; the page discloses this in a prominent note, so the gap is honest rather than hidden.

interactive.rationale: The run button executes both shapes for real against /public/echo-socket and times them; verified 6.1ms handshake-carried vs 3.7ms first-message with a measured 1.3ms unproven-session window.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The card promises both shapes run and timed with the server-trust framing, which the page delivers, stand-in disclosed.

edge_cases.rationale: Loopback timing inversion is anticipated in the narration ('ordering can invert — latency is the small difference'), and endpoint failure has an explicit error path.

conformance.rationale: The suite covers the real API contracts (headers member read, responseHeaders on the prototype, forbidden-name guard); on Chromium 141 it honestly ran 5 pass / 2 fail with exactly the two Chrome-154 assertions failing.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp): both shapes completed against this origin with real timings and the unproven-window measurement; console clean, no failed same-origin requests, desktop and mobile screenshots read.

telemetry_health.rationale: Loads demo-telemetry.js and logs handshake/firstMessage/unproven timings.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables, figures with shape diagrams, captioned results table, no static card.

accessibility.rationale: aria-live detail, captioned table with scoped headers, figures paired with text explanations.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: No horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3 (scrollWidth 360, screenshot read).

openQuestions.title: Attempt a real WebTransport connection when the environment allows it
openQuestions.detail: The WebSocket stand-in is honestly disclosed and the shape argument holds, but on a Chrome 154+ visitor over a host with HTTP/3 the page could additionally attempt new WebTransport(url, { headers }) against a public echo endpoint (or degrade with the current note when none is reachable), so at least one row of the measurement uses the actual API this feature ships. Keep the stand-in as the always-works path.

summary: Reviewed at http://localhost:3000/v154/webtransport-headers-and-responseheaders/auth-at-connect/ with Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp). Both authentication shapes ran for real and were timed (6.1ms vs 3.7ms with a 1.3ms unproven-session window), the loopback-inversion caveat is pre-empted in the copy, and the page carries a prominent note that the transport is a WebSocket stand-in because this host cannot serve HTTP/3 — the honest version of an infrastructure constraint. Console/network clean bar the sandbox font-CDN artifact; no mobile overflow; feature /conformance/ honestly ran 5 pass / 2 fail (the two Chrome-154 assertions). One minor enhancement: attempt the real API when environment permits.
